## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change to `app/report.py:5` is correct: an exact match on `"REPORT v1"` rejects other versions like `REPORT v0`. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers that branch. However, `test_rejects_legacy_header` never builds a legacy header, so it cannot catch the defect its name and comment describe. The policy manifest lists no policy files.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `"v0".join(fixture.rsplit("v1", 1))` replaces only the last `v1`, so `legacy` becomes `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. The header is still `REPORT v1` and the body has no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at the `lines[-1] != "END"` check in `app/report.py:3` and never reaches the version check. The comment on line 9, "changing the fixture's version to v0", is also false for this reason. Could you use a complete report with a v0 header instead, e.g. `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or delete this test, since line 16 already covers that case? — The test passes even if the header check at `app/report.py:5` is removed or put back to `startswith("REPORT ")`, so it adds false coverage for the regression it is named after.

(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_report.py:15-17` uses a complete report with a `REPORT v0` header. That test fails under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check and passes under the new exact match, so it does exercise the changed branch.
